FUTURE OUTLOOK
During the dynamic and challenging microeconomic
environment, the Company has delivered another
sound financial and operational performance during FY
2025-26. The Company is remaining focused on driving
sustainable growth and expanding its exports and
footprint in electronics manufacturing services (EMS).
Dixon’s broader strategy is to evolve from a scale led EMS
player to a moat driven electronics Company by ensuing
expansion into ODM based solutions by building design,
engineering and prototyping capabilities, increasing
share of wallet by expanding the product basket for
existing customers and leveraging existing product
platforms to onboard new customers for same products
and driving scale efficiencies. To ensure operational
excellence, the Company is looking to ensure end-to-end
digitalization for faster and data driven decision making.
By leveraging the manufacturing scale, Dixon is deepening
the value addition by strategic captive investments in
critical components such as Display, Camera Modules,
Mechanicals, SSDs etc. Moreover, the Company plans
to leverage its strong financial position and operational
capabilities to capitalize on emerging opportunities and
cater to the evolving needs of the Customers.
In the Home Appliances business vertical, the Company
is looking to expand into new product categories such
as Fully Automatic Front Load Washing Machine (FAFL),
dishwashers, microwaves & other kitchen appliances
etc. and exploring injection moulding for mobile phones,
laptops etc.
In the Mobile business vertical, the Company is looking for
volume expansion, ramping up of operations, expanding
exports across key markets and using backward
integration capabilities to offer an integrated box building
and key components propositions.
In the Consumer Electronics business vertical, the
Company is moving towards expansion of its customer
base in Interactive Flat Panel Displays (IFPD) and Digital
Signage segments and expansion of exports across
major key markets.
Dixon remains strongly focused on quality, manufacturing
excellence and consistently meeting the requirements
of its key customers, while reinforcing its position as a
leading player in the EMS industry. Dixon is optimistic
about the opportunities ahead and confident in its ability
to maintain its leadership as India’s premier electronics
manufacturing services Company, while delivering
steady growth in revenue and profitability.

BOARD EVALUATION PROCESS
The Board had carried out an annual evaluation of its
own performance and of its committees as well as
the performance of each individual Directors. Board
Evaluation Criteria Feedback was sought based on the
evaluation criteria approved by the NRC for evaluating the
performance of the Board, its committees and individual
directors. The Executive Chairman, Vice Chairman &
Managing Director and the Independent Directors were
evaluated on the following parameters:
1. The Board – Board Administration, Overall Board
Effectiveness, Governance and Compliance, Member
Effectiveness, Ethics, Chairman, Board Committees,
Meeting through Video Conferencing, Miscellaneous.
2. Board committees – Committee Effectiveness
Component including the frequency of the
meetings, the chairperson of the Committee, the
time allotted for agenda items, proper agenda
papers and other required documents, healthy
debates and discussions, action taken points from
the previous committee meetings, information flow,
recommendations to the Board, etc.
3. Executive Directors – Attendance at the meetings,
engagement with fellow Board members, employees,
strategy making, risk management, management of
the company and its employees.
4. The Chairman – Leadership of the Board, promoting
effective participation of all Board members in the
decision-making process, encouraging deliberations
on important matters etc.
5. Independent Directors – Independence from the
Company, exercising independent judgement
in decision-making, contributing strongly to the
objectivity of the Board’s deliberations based on
their external expertise, attendance at meetings etc.
In order to ensure confidentiality, the Board’s evaluation
was undertaken by way of a questionnaire circulated
through an online tool by an independent agency. All
the directors participated in the evaluation process.
The responses received from the Board members were
compiled by an independent agency and a consolidated
report was submitted by the agency to the Board through
the Company Secretary.
The evaluation report was also discussed at the meeting
of the Board of Directors. The Board deliberated over the
suggestions and inputs to augment its own effectiveness
and optimise the individual strengths of the directors. The
directors were satisfied with the Company’s standard
of governance, its transparency, meeting practices and
overall Board effectiveness.
The suggestions given by the Independent Directors were
duly incorporated.
